continuity.narrative_arc: Rasa-dance bliss turns to pride and Krishna’s disappearance; he takes Radha aside, the gopikas search and question the trees, imagine his presence and imitate him, then lament until Krishna reappears and joy returns.
continuity.krishna_identity: Depict the Vrindavan gopi-period Krishna as the same serene youthful cowherd seen in primary identity references D066 S002 v004 and D066 S010 v004: calm almond eyes, deep matte blue skin, long dark curly hair, yellow dhoti, muted red-orange shawl, a simple low gold band with one upright peacock feather, and a plain smooth forehead. He is youthful, not an infant. Secondary D066 S004 and S008 references guide the face only, never the forehead. Recompose the new scene; do not copy a reference pose or background.
continuity.gopika_contract: Use the existing gopikas character bible: distinct adult women with natural proportions and simple village dress. For every D066 scene, keep them modestly and fully clothed in opaque garments. The clothing-promise verse is represented symbolically; never depict undressing, nudity, exposed bodies, sexualized framing, or a clothing theft in progress.
continuity.deity_contract: All physical narrative appearances show one youthful, deep-blue, two-armed Krishna. Stanza 6 alone may include one small imagined Krishna image, explicitly nonphysical and visually separated from the gopika.
continuity.radha_contract: Radha, an adult gopika, distinct from the unnamed group; calm and without pride in stanza 3, later sorrowful after separation in stanza 7.
